Reused declaration: this is the comparator-accepted theorem Submission.cmr_cc_det_covector_exists (DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.mass_representation-a1.coordinate_covectors-a1.det_covector_exists-a1) with byte-identical frozen type; no new formal work is needed. Its accepted proof is reproduced here.

Notation: ℝ^P := Euclid P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P); for x ∈ ℝ^P and l ∈ Fin P, x(l) (Lean: x l) is the l-th coordinate of x; an n-covector is an element of Covector (Euclid P) n = (Euclid P) [⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ.

1. (Coordinate projection.) Fix P, n and I : Fin n → Fin P. Define p_I : ℝ^P → (Fin n → ℝ) by p_I(x) := (fun k => x(I k)). Since (x + y)(l) = x(l) + y(l) and (c•x)(l) = c·x(l), p_I is ℝ-linear.
2. (Determinant as an alternating map.) Θ := Matrix.detRowAlternating : (Fin n → ℝ) [⋀^Fin n]→ₗ[ℝ] ℝ is alternating and multilinear, Θ(u) = det(Matrix.of u). Put θ⁰ := Θ.compLinearMap p_I. By AlternatingMap.compLinearMap_apply, θ⁰(v) = det(Matrix.of fun j k => v j (I k)) for every v : Fin n → ℝ^P.
3. (Transpose.) The transpose of Matrix.of fun j k => v j (I k) is Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k); since det Mᵀ = det M (Matrix.det_transpose), θ⁰(v) = det(Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k)).
4. (Multiplicative bound.) Let M := Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k). By the Leibniz formula (Matrix.det_apply) det M = Σ_σ sign(σ)·Π_j v_j(I(σ j)). By the triangle inequality, |sign σ| = 1 and |v_j(l)| ≤ ‖v_j‖ (PiLp.norm_apply_le), |det M| ≤ Σ_σ Π_j ‖v_j‖ = n!·Π_j ‖v_j‖ (Fintype.card_perm).
5. (Continuity and conclusion.) By step 4, AlternatingMap.mkContinuous applies to θ⁰ with constant n!; θ := θ⁰.mkContinuous n! (bound of step 4) is an n-covector whose underlying function is that of θ⁰, so θ(v) = det(Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k)) for every v by step 3.
6. (Degenerate cases.) No property of I was used; for n = 0, Perm(Fin 0) has one element, the empty product is 1 and θ is the constant 1, the determinant of the empty matrix.
proof_key_steps: p_I x := (x(I k))_k is linear; θ⁰ := Matrix.detRowAlternating.compLinearMap p_I is alternating n-linear.
Matrix.det_transpose rewrites θ⁰ v as det(Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k)).
Leibniz, |x(l)| ≤ ‖x‖ and card Perm(Fin n) = n! give |θ⁰ v| ≤ n!·Π_j ‖v_j‖.
θ := θ⁰.mkContinuous n! is the required n-covector.

subproblems.title: Coordinate expansion of a k-covector: k!·f(u) = Σ_I f(e'_I)·det(u_b(I_c))

Write e'_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i ∈ Fin N') for the standard basis of ℝ^{N'} and z(i) for the i-th coordinate of z ∈ ℝ^{N'}. Then k!·f(u) = Σ_{I : Fin k → Fin N'} f(e'_{I(0)}, …, e'_{I(k−1)})·det(M_I), where the sum runs over all maps I (no monotonicity or injectivity) and M_I is the k×k matrix with entry u_b(I(c)) in row c and column b (Lean: Matrix.of fun c b => u b (I c)).

Source: parent Step 2 ('Write ω = Σ_I ω_I dy^{I_1} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dy^{I_k} ... Then H^#ω(u)(e) = Σ_I ω_I(H(u))·det D(H^I)(u) (multilinearity and alternation of dy^I ∘ DH(u))'), stated pointwise for one covector f (the parent uses f = ω(H(u)) and u_b = DH(u)e_b) and summed over all index maps I instead of increasing ones; each increasing I then occurs k! times, which produces the factor k!.

Notation. ℝ^{N'} = Euclid N'; e'_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i ∈ Fin N'); z(i) (Lean z i) is the i-th coordinate of z ∈ ℝ^{N'}. For I : Fin k → Fin N' put e'_I := (e'_{I(0)}, …, e'_{I(k−1)}) and let M_I be the k×k matrix with (M_I)_{c,b} = u_b(I(c)).

1. (Basis expansion.) Every z ∈ ℝ^{N'} satisfies z = Σ_{i ∈ Fin N'} z(i)·e'_i (the standard basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun has the coordinates as its repr; Basis.sum_repr). In particular u_b = Σ_i u_b(i)·e'_i for every b.
2. (Multilinear expansion.) f is multilinear, so (MultilinearMap.map_sum) f(u) = f(Σ_i u_0(i)e'_i, …, Σ_i u_{k−1}(i)e'_i) = Σ_{J : Fin k → Fin N'} f(u_0(J 0)·e'_{J 0}, …, u_{k−1}(J(k−1))·e'_{J(k−1)}), and pulling out the scalars (MultilinearMap.map_smul_univ) each summand equals (Π_b u_b(J b))·f(e'_J). Hence f(u) = Σ_J (Π_b u_b(J b))·f(e'_J).
3. (Reindexing by a permutation.) Fix σ ∈ Perm(Fin k). The map I ↦ I ∘ σ is a bijection of the finite set of maps Fin k → Fin N' (inverse J ↦ J ∘ σ⁻¹; Lean Equiv.arrowCongr σ⁻¹ (Equiv.refl _)). Substituting J = I ∘ σ in step 2: f(u) = Σ_I (Π_b u_b(I(σ b)))·f(e'_{I(σ 0)}, …, e'_{I(σ(k−1))}).
4. (Alternation.) The family (e'_{I(σ b)})_b is the family e'_I composed with σ, and an alternating map satisfies f(v ∘ σ) = sign(σ)·f(v) (AlternatingMap.map_perm). Hence, for every σ, f(u) = Σ_I sign(σ)·(Π_b u_b(I(σ b)))·f(e'_I).
5. (Averaging.) Perm(Fin k) has k! elements (Fintype.card_perm). Summing step 4 over all σ and exchanging the two finite sums: k!·f(u) = Σ_σ f(u) = Σ_I f(e'_I)·Σ_σ sign(σ)·Π_b u_b(I(σ b)).
6. (Leibniz formula.) By Matrix.det_apply, det M_I = Σ_σ sign(σ)·Π_b (M_I)_{σ(b), b} = Σ_σ sign(σ)·Π_b u_b(I(σ b)). Substituting into step 5 gives k!·f(u) = Σ_I f(e'_I)·det M_I, the claim.
7. (Degenerate cases.) Steps 1–6 use neither k ≥ 1 nor N' ≥ 1. For k = 0 there is exactly one I (the empty map), 0! = 1, the empty determinant is 1 and f(e'_I) = f(u) (both arguments are the empty family). For N' = 0 < k the right side is an empty sum and step 2 gives f(u) = 0.

The determinant is a polynomial in the entries (Leibniz formula: a finite sum of ± products of entries), so every M_b is C¹. Consequently F_b := ψ·g_0·M_b is C¹ and has compact support (its support lies in that of ψ).
3. (Product rule.) ∂_{V_b}F_b = ∂_{V_b}ψ·g_0·M_b + ψ·∂_{V_b}g_0·M_b + ψ·g_0·∂_{V_b}M_b.

The middle terms give ψ·Σ_b (−1)^b ∂_{V_b}g_0·M_b = ψ·det A by step 1, and the last terms give ψ·g_0·Σ_b (−1)^b ∂_{V_b}M_b = 0 by step 4.
